title: DurableJobPartialRetryContractDraft
description: Draft schema and behavioral contract for durable batch jobs supporting JobStatus.PARTIAL, itemized receipts, and member-level idempotency/retry.

status_orthogonality.business_outcome: JobStatus: QUEUED | RUNNING | SUCCEEDED | FAILED | CANCELLED | PARTIAL
status_orthogonality.rule: JobStatus represents business outcome; JobDeliveryState represents queue delivery mechanics. In the existing system, normal success writes SUCCEEDED with delivery_state=null, active retries write QUEUED with delivery_state=RETRYING, and terminal failures write FAILED paired with delivery_state=DEAD_LETTER upon retry exhaustion or non-retryable errors. For multi-item batch jobs completing as PARTIAL, transport delivery is finished, so delivery_state is cleared (set to null), cleanly separating business partial completion from infrastructure dead-lettering without allowing transport delivery states to overwrite business outcome.

state_transition_rules.single_item_jobs: Must transition strictly to SUCCEEDED or FAILED (never PARTIAL).
batch_multi_item_precedence_rules: 1. Empty batch precedence: If total_count == 0 => JobStatus.SUCCEEDED (with succeeded_count = 0, failed_count = 0, cancelled_count = 0, pending_count = 0).
2. Non-finalization rule: If pending_count > 0 => Job remains in active non-terminal state (JobStatus.RUNNING or JobStatus.QUEUED); pending items MUST NOT finalize the job into a terminal state.
3. Cancellation precedence: If cancelled_count > 0 or job was aborted by operator/system => JobStatus.CANCELLED (takes unambiguous precedence over partial counts).
4. All Succeeded: If succeeded_count == total_count and total_count > 0 and failed_count == 0 and cancelled_count == 0 and pending_count == 0 => JobStatus.SUCCEEDED.
5. All Failed: If failed_count == total_count and total_count > 0 and succeeded_count == 0 and cancelled_count == 0 and pending_count == 0 => JobStatus.FAILED.
6. Mixed Partial Outcome: If succeeded_count > 0 and failed_count > 0 and cancelled_count == 0 and pending_count == 0 => JobStatus.PARTIAL.

scoped_retry_policy.execution_behavior: Engine reads previous ItemReceipt items; items with item_status == 'SUCCEEDED' are skipped with zero downstream invocations; items with item_status == 'FAILED' and error.retryable == false are permanent bad input and skipped with zero downstream invocations (attempt count unchanged); only items with item_status == 'FAILED' and error.retryable == true are re-executed (attempt incremented by 1).
scoped_retry_policy.convergence_rule: Retried items that succeed update item_status to SUCCEEDED and increment attempt. When all originally failed items reach SUCCEEDED, the aggregate JobStatus converges from PARTIAL to SUCCEEDED. If non-retryable failed items remain, the aggregate JobStatus remains PARTIAL with updated summary counts.

replay_identity_and_ordering.purpose: Defines replay identity and stale-result handling so that duplicate message delivery and out-of-order attempt completion cannot corrupt a PARTIAL aggregate. Retry alone is not sufficient: the FAILED_ONLY scoped retry in scoped_retry_policy is a single sequential operation and by construction cannot detect a duplicated delivery of the same attempt, nor an older attempt's result arriving after a newer attempt already succeeded.
replay_identity_and_ordering.job_replay_identity: A durable job is identified for replay by job_id. Client-facing enqueue deduplication uses idempotency_key, already implemented at DurableJobQueue.enqueue (shared/infrastructure/persistence/job_queue.py:65-110) via INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING followed by an idempotency_key readback that returns (existing_record, created=False). Re-enqueuing the same idempotency_key must therefore never create a second job and never reset an existing aggregate.
replay_identity_and_ordering.item_replay_identity: An item execution is identified by the triple (job_id, item_id, attempt). item_id is unique within the job; attempt is the monotonically increasing execution counter already present on ItemReceipt. A per-item idempotency_key (ItemReceipt.idempotency_key) identifies the downstream business write so that the downstream side can also reject a replay. The triple is the fencing token for applying any item result.
replay_identity_and_ordering.apply_once_rule: A result for (job_id, item_id, attempt) is applied at most once. On receiving a result whose triple has already been applied, the engine performs no downstream write, does not increment attempt, does not modify counts in JobSummary, and does not rewrite last_attempt_at. The duplicate is acknowledged and discarded.
replay_identity_and_ordering.stale_result_rule: A result is stale, and must be discarded without any state change, when either: (a) its attempt is lower than the attempt currently recorded on the ItemReceipt; or (b) the ItemReceipt is already in item_status == 'SUCCEEDED'. In particular a late-arriving failure from an older attempt must never overwrite a SUCCEEDED item_status, must never null out an existing result_ref, and must never re-populate error on a succeeded item.
replay_identity_and_ordering.monotonicity_rule: attempt is non-decreasing per item. item_status transitions out of SUCCEEDED are forbidden for the same job run; SUCCEEDED is terminal at item level. result_ref, once set on a SUCCEEDED item, is immutable.
replay_identity_and_ordering.aggregate_derivation_rule: JobSummary counts and the aggregate JobStatus are derived deterministically from the persisted ItemReceipt set by applying state_transition_rules.batch_multi_item_precedence_rules. They are never incremented ad hoc by message handling. Consequently the final aggregate is a pure function of the item receipts and is identical after a restart, and identical regardless of the arrival order or multiplicity of duplicate messages.
replay_identity_and_ordering.cancellation_interaction: The stale_result_rule applies to cancellation as well: a result arriving for an item already recorded CANCELLED with attempt == 0 (cancelled before execution) must not resurrect that item to SUCCEEDED or FAILED; it is discarded and reported as a stale-delivery observation.
replay_identity_and_ordering.scope_note: This is an A-stage contract and test specification only. No implementation and no test execution is performed or claimed by ODP-DURABLE-PARTIAL-CONTRACT-PREP-001; the corresponding acceptance cases are specified in implementation-handoff.md section 4 test 5 and are WP-33B work.

code.description: Machine-readable error code (e.g. MISSING_MANDATORY_ADDRESS, GEOCODING_UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT, CANCELLED_BEFORE_EXECUTION)

retryable.description: True if transient failure eligible for retry; false if permanent bad input or deterministic rejection

item_id.description: Unique identifier of the item within the job (e.g. row-001, loc-42)

item_status.description: Terminal or lifecycle outcome for this specific member

attempt.description: Total execution attempts made for this item (0 for unstarted PENDING or pre-execution CANCELLED items; >=1 for items that executed at least once)

result_ref.description: Pointer to created resource or receipt (e.g. intake-991823); null for failed, cancelled, or pending items

idempotency_key.description: Per-item client idempotency key if supplied

last_attempt_at.description: Timestamp of last execution attempt, or null if attempt == 0

total_count.description: Sum of succeeded_count + failed_count + cancelled_count + pending_count

job_id.description: Global unique identifier of the durable job
